scope: Physical R131 shared-path completion supplement; independent recomputation from raw operation latencies and process CPU clocks

decision.rule: All correctness/identity/cleanup gates required. No regression gate passes if any lane/metric has all six paired R131/R124 deltas positive and median greater than +5%. Ratios within ±1% treated as engineering ties; no claim of equivalence.
decision.disposition: R131 not accepted as final ubusd; preserve measured event gains and shared-path regression together

caller_timing.latency: Instant before add_object through successful remove_object; includes client encoding, IPC, daemon processing, and scheduling
caller_timing.percentile: sorted sample index floor((n-1)*q+0.5), n=5000; p95 index=4749, zero based
caller_timing.daemon_cpu: first monitored PID process CPU delta over measured loop, divided by 5000
caller_timing.caller_cpu: benchmark process CPU clock delta over measured loop, divided by 5000
caller_timing.bounds: preflight signature validation and final empty lookup outside timing; each timed cycle still validates ADD id and successful statuses
caller_timing.instrument_identity: same benchmark ELF, count, flags, CPU masks, and daemon argv0 for every subject

observations: Both registration p95 guards fail the frozen six-positive-pairs and >5% paired-median rule.
register_16_8 median +5.0085% is only slightly above the threshold; it is still a failure under the frozen rule.
R131 window 13 has elevated daemon involuntary context switches (259 for register_1_8), consistent with scheduling interference but not proof of its cause.
All six register_1_8 p95 and daemon CPU pairs rise, including the other five blocks; no post-hoc window exclusion is applied.
Temperature is approximately 60C and does not show a simple monotonic drift matching these peaks.
No artifact, CPU affinity, process identity, sample-count, cleanup, or arithmetic failure was found.
R131 changes dispatch_event setup also reached by object add/remove with no receivers; the slowdown is not attributed to a specific instruction without a profile.
limits: Engineering regression guard, not a population effect-size confidence claim.
Tail timing includes caller and scheduling; raw p95 changes cannot be called daemon-only latency regression.
No per-symbol profile or router CPU-frequency trace in this workload; exact causal attribution remains open.
No threshold changes, data exclusion, or rerun was used.
